EmailTemplate.subject: Thank you for your interest in graduate studies at ASU!
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear {!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in graduate studies at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts School of Music at ASU. As one of the largest universities in the country, the ASU School of Music awards over $2 million to students annually, providing an excellent education at an unbeatable value. ASU's diverse and innovative community is a perfect complement to the personal attention you will receive in the School of Music. With a population of around 750 students, we offer small class sizes, state-of-the-art facilities and one-on-one instruction from world-renowned faculty. We invite you to consider the ASU School of Music for this important step in your music studies.
Applications for 2017 admission will be available on the School of Music website in August. If you are interested in future study at ASU, please review the information below as guidelines for what to expect when you are ready to apply. For an idea of the course requirements for the various degree programs offered, select one of the checksheets accessible by your degree program interest here.
Tuition and fees at Arizona State University are reasonable, even for non-resident students. Music Scholarships and teaching assistantships are available. Typical assistantships are 25% which amount to 10 hours or work per week and receive:
Tuition remission covering the non-resident portion of tuition 50% reduction in the resident portion of tuition (excluding fees) $7,450 stipend for the academic year, distributed over bi-weekly paychecks
Spoken English requirement: If your native language is not English you must meet spoken English requirements before you can be considered for teaching assistantship. You may complete the ASU SPEAK test (minimum score of 55).Those wishing to be considered for Graduate Teaching Assistantships should submit a TA application by February 15 for an appointment beginning Fall semester.
Application Process
Step 1: You must first submit the Graduate Admissions application, followed by the School of Music application, before an audition or interview will be scheduled.
Step 2: All transcripts and test scores must be submitted directly to the Graduate Admissions Office of the University.
Step 3: Auditions or Interviews will be scheduled and application materials will be reviewed only after all application materials have been submitted. We are not responsible for application materials sent to the wrong office or directly to faculty. Please check the Graduate Education website for application information, and the School of Music website for specific application requirements for your degree program.
Applicants to the PhD Music Education must submit GRE scores. The GRE examination in Music is not acceptable for admission to the doctoral program. GRE scores must be from within 5 years prior to the first day of the enrollment term.
Due to the high volume of applicants we receive each year, we recommend that you plan to apply as early as possible.
Rolling Application deadlines: Applications to the graduate program in music therapy and music education are accepted until all spaces are filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible and before February 28 for Fall admission if they wish to be considered for scholarship. While applications will continue to be accepted, scholarships may not be available after March. To ensure prompt processing of your application, please email MusicAdmissions@asu.edu after you have submitted your application.
We welcome you to contact us via email to MusicAdmissions@asu.edu if you have any additional questions. We also encourage you to refer to the School of Music Web site, music.asu.edu, as a resource for your admissions questions.
Sincerely,
Office of Admissions School of Music
Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts Arizona State University
